problems.issue: EEG abnormalities are entirely absent from simulated true and reported phenotypes despite being reported in 88% of R1-train patients. This omits a central diagnostic feature of this epilepsy syndrome.

Example 1 is dominated by unrelated findings: retinal dystrophy, underdeveloped nasal alae, lower-limb hyporeflexia, and psoriasiform dermatitis. With only one seizure feature and no developmental phenotype, it would teach a misleading disease signature.

Epileptic encephalopathy is reported in only 36% of simulations versus 71% of R1-train patients, underrepresenting the defining phenotype despite substantial reporting of seizures and developmental impairment.

summary: The predominant seizure and developmental features are broadly plausible, but missing EEG abnormalities and the unrelated findings dominating example 1 make the simulated cohort clinically implausible. Age and sex differences alone are not clearly problematic.
